searchText: I use a variation of this <https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial/pull/28> whenever I need to send thousands of deposits. I think <@199561711278227457> has good scripts and probably `ethdo` or `ethereal` can send deposits now The execution layer "testing" channel is pretty focused. I suspect that it will be disruptive to them if we join them. I believe that we can just remove the one under merge You can generate the deposits with `eth2-val-tools` and then submit them with `ethereal`, that's usually the process I follow on testnets 🙂 It seems like there would be significant value in an IPFS hosted UI that makes zero external requests and allows the user to specify their EL (e.g., http://localhost:8545) and it provides the user with a nice UI. Would be cool if it *also* had an option to generate the transactions and write them to a file for the user (for airgapped signing). Bonus points if the same page lets you *load* a file generated by the page, so you can just load the same page on your online device, load the file your air gapped device generated, and click submit. I don't think this is useful. Most people (if not all) submitting thousand of deposits are devs testing. At the moment, I think the only way for an end-user to stake (realistically) is via launchpad.ethereum.org which I don't believe works offline/airgapped (please correct me if I'm wrong)? The launchpad does not need to be airgapped at all, it takes only public information And then to deposit is just a regular ETH transfer or contract call using the wallet of your choice? Yes The UX is awkward if you need to approve manually a thousand transfers, but I think users that need to deposit 32 thousand ETH can afford to pay someone to send the deposits
